newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Q3 trading conditions flat - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Q3 trading conditions flat - survey.

text.p: Business trading conditions in Australia remained subdued in the September quarter, according to a National Australia Bank (NAB) survey released on Monday.

The NAB Quarterly Business survey said it was the second consecutive fall in trading conditions. The result defied expectations for a significant improvement in conditions during the September quarter, as reported in the previous survey.

The September report found profitability remained poor and there was a small fall in employment - the first since late 1993. Forward orders declined for the sixth consecutive quarter, while stocks increased contrary to expectations of a rundown.
"The marked slowing in price pressures from an already low level continued in the September quarter," the survey said.

The bank said businesses surveyed reported price increases of only 0.3 percent in the quarter, in line with the June quarter result. However, businesses remained optimistic about the current quarter, saying they expected trading conditions to improve slightly in the three months to December.

"Looking ahead, most respondents are more optimistic for the next quarter, but given poor forward orders and a recent history of disappointment, not too much should be read into this," NAB chief economist Alan Oster said in a commentary.
"Looking further ahead, respondents revised downwards their 12 month outlook for business conditions - mainly in the areas of employment and capital expenditure," he said.

But Oster said long-term inflationary expectations had improved with 89 percent of respondents expecting inflation to be less than four percent for the remainder of the 1990s. This compared to 79 percent of respondents in the June quarter.
Oster said most respondents also expected interest rates to remain unchanged or to decline over the next 12 months.
NAB had lowered its growth forecast to about 2.4 percent for 1996/97 from 2.75 percent previously and said there was further scope for an interest rate cut, possibly as early as November.
